To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the efficiency of exciplex lasers with large apertures is determined by the parasitic amplification coefficient of the spontaneous radiation, which depends on the aperture, the reflectivity of the mirrors, and the reflectivity of laser tube walls.
the radiation characteristics of a large-aperture excimer laser with plane mirrors are described well by the transfer equation approximation.
the efficiency of an exciplex laser with large apertures can be improved by increasing the coefficient of reflection of the mirrors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis and optimization of exciplex laser radiation systems with apertures of 10 to 50 cm.
the development of a theoretical basis for the optimization of the parameters of exciplex lasers and amplifiers.
a theoretical investigation of the radiation characteristics in large-aperture excimer lasers and amplifiers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the present study can be used to optimize exciplex laser designs and to improve the efficiency and the beam quality of the radiation.
a laser with an aperture of 0.5-1 m and with a mirror reflectance of 0.9-0.99 can be used to produce a laser pulse with an energy of 0.1-10 J.
the use of exciplex lasers with plane mirrors is not promising for the production of high-power laser radiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a method that makes it possible to calculate the radiation characteristics of laser systems in the transfer equation approach and have applied this method to a number of practical problems.
the results of the calculations of the radiation characteristics are in satisfactory agreement with the experimental data.

the use of the transfer equation approximation in the analysis of exciplex laser radiation characteristics makes it possible to predict the behavior of the system in a fairly wide range of parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the divergence of the radiation from the laser and the amplifier is determined by the divergence of the spontaneous radiation and by the coefficient of reflection in the active medium, while the energy characteristics of the system are determined mainly by the mirror reflection coefficient.
the radiation characteristics of the exciplex laser can be improved by using a telescopic system with a high coefficient of reflection of the walls of the amplifier.

the use of mirrors with a high coefficient of reflection by an exciplex laser with a large-aperture active medium can significantly improve the efficiency of the system and reduce the divergence of the radiation, while the use of a telescopic system can increase the efficiency of the amplifier.
